summary.headline: JNK India Q4 FY26 revenue rose 69.2% YoY to Rs 344.6 crore, with EBITDA margin at 15.2%; FY27 revenue growth guided at 25-30%.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was Rs 344.6 crore (+69.2% YoY), with EBITDA of Rs 52.3 crore (+89.9%) at a 15.2% margin and PAT of Rs 33 crore (+149.5%). FY26 revenue reached Rs 838 crore (+68%), PAT Rs 64.8 crore (+114.6%), and the order book ended the year at Rs 1,961.4 crore after Rs 1,694.4 crore of FY26 inflows. Management attributed margin expansion mainly to project mix (legacy orders completed in Q1-Q2) and guided 14-15% EBITDA margin as sustainable. Management guided FY27 revenue growth of 25-30%, with Dangote refinery and fertilizer reformer awards as key near-term catalysts.

financial_highlights.metric: FY26 order inflow / order book (31 Mar 2026)

segments.name: Heating equipment
segments.commentary: Contributed 72.7% of FY26 revenue and about 94% of order book value.

segments.name: Process plant
segments.commentary: Contributed 17.4% of FY26 revenue and 3.5% of order book.

segments.name: Special fabricated equipment
segments.commentary: Contributed 3.1% of FY26 revenue and 1.3% of order book; described as a new segment.

segments.name: Flares, incinerators and others
segments.commentary: Contributed 6.3% of FY26 revenue and about 1.2% of order book.

segments.name: JNK Chemdist Technologies (JV)
segments.commentary: Contributed about 7% of group revenue in roughly six months of its first year; JV order backlog about Rs 67-70 crore, bid pipeline about Rs 200 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at around 25-30% YoY, implying roughly Rs 1,050-1,090 crore on the FY26 base; management also called 25-30% feasible for FY28.
EBITDA margin expected in the 14-15% range going forward, based on Q3 and Q4 FY26 run-rate, with conservatism due to commodity price risk.
Revenue phasing: Q1 expected to be lowest, Q4 highest; H2 expected at roughly 40-60% of FY27 revenue.
Order book expected to cross about Rs 2,000 crore by end of FY27.
Operating cash flow expected to remain positive in FY27, though not on a large scale.
Dangote refinery fired heater award expected in Q1 FY27 and reformer award in Q2 or Q3 FY27; fertilizer reformer bid submission in Q1 with finalisation in Q2 or Q3.
Waste gas handling package at export expected to close within one to two weeks; clean aviation fuel bid lost (not lowest bidder).
Chemdist expected to add 10-15% of group revenue in the first couple of years.
capex_capacity: No major capex planned; management said FY27 growth needs little capex.
Planned smaller domestic facility for critical fabrication and storage, capex about Rs 10-15 crore; current facility is mainly export-oriented.
About 120 in-house engineers; fabrication outsourced to approved shops near sites, specialised bought-out items sourced from approved Indian suppliers.
Capacity constrained by manpower in engineering, procurement and project management, and by working capital; management said no meaningful capacity utilisation metric exists.
Current order book expected to be executed over roughly two years.
demand_pricing: Order book Rs 1,961.4 crore: 97.5% India, 2.5% international; JV (Chemdist) about Rs 67-70 crore, JNK India about Rs 1,890 crore, legacy about Rs 40-50 crore.
Bid pipeline about Rs 4,000 crore: about Rs 1,500 crore on JNK India alone and Rs 2,500-3,000 crore alongside JNK Global; conversion rate 25-30%, targeting Rs 1,300-1,500 crore inflows.

Dangote Phase 2 refinery: both inquiries received and JNK prequalified for fired heaters and reformers (and flares); competitors include other European players and Chinese bidders; combined bid with JNK Global as main bidder.
Export opportunities of about Rs 4,000 crore in Africa, Middle East and Russia; Middle East fertilizer/petchem opportunity of $200-300 million over two to three years.
Domestic refinery/petchem projects (BPCL Andhra, IOCL Paradip, Haldia) expected to take six months to a year due to crude pricing pressures; cracking furnace order opportunity likely in FY28.
Commodity pricing: generally no pass-through clauses except limited PSU contracts; procurement placed within one to two months of contract award.
Royalty: technical fee up to 2% of order value on exports booked in JNK India's name for items common with JNK Global.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the margin expansion was project mix, and what is the normalised EBITDA run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said EBITDA was about 7% in Q1, 12% in Q2, 14% in Q3 and above 15% in Q4 due to legacy project completion and new projects on input accounting; 14-15% is the normal range.

qa_highlights.question: Has EIL issued RFQs for Dangote Phase 2, and is JNK prequalified?
qa_highlights.answer: Both inquiries received and prequalified for fired heaters and reformers, plus flares; fired heater award expected Q1 FY27, reformer Q2 or Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Will operating cash flow turn positive?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said operating cash flow is already positive, though modest; improvement driven by private and export customers with better down payments versus PSU orders.

qa_highlights.question: Why is operating cash flow negative and how long does unbilled revenue take to convert?
qa_highlights.answer: Unbilled revenue mainly from new cracker furnace and process plant projects with private customers; expected to convert to cash in about three months.

qa_highlights.question: Can execution capacity support Rs 2,000-2,500 crore annual revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth needs balancing capability, handling and working capital; 25-30% annual growth appears feasible, with capacity built year on year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Chemdist green hydrogen technology and pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Technology produces hydrogen as a by-product from green ethanol to ethyl acetate using a special catalyst; first project from Hydrogen Valley Pune, Rs 70 crore backlog; commercial-scale proof targeted next year. Standalone solar EPC not planned.

risks_watch: Commodity price volatility and geopolitical disruption to imports and exports; limited pass-through clauses on contracts.
Operating cash flow still negative in the last three years; working capital needs rising with project scale.
Revenue concentration: about 97.5% of order book is domestic and about Rs 1,600 crore of the order book is linked to BPCL Bina via JNK Global.
Dangote and reformer award timing (Q1-Q3 FY27) and competition from European and other bidders; clean aviation fuel bid lost.
Heavy H2 weighting (about 65% of FY26 revenue) and Q1 seasonality.
Chemdist technology not yet commercially proven; margin uplift from JV deferred by a couple of years.
summary.management_tone: Confident on near-term order wins and the 25-30% FY27 growth outlook, but cautious on margins and domestic refinery timelines, citing crude pricing and geopolitical risk. Management was candid when correcting analyst assumptions (H1/H2 split, cracking furnace timing) and avoided firm numbers on commodity exposure.
key_quotes: So, 14% to 15% is what basically is the normal EBITDA, what going forward also, we should expect in this range.
Hence, we expect a revenue growth of around 25% to 30% in FY27.
So, considering all this, we feel the EBITDA margin of 14% to 15% is more sustainable.
Generally, we do not have the clauses to pass it on to the customer.

adds.what: Planned smaller domestic facility for critical fabrication and storage

growth.why: Management guides FY27 revenue growth of 25-30% (about Rs 1,050-1,090 crore on the Rs 838 crore FY26 base), backed by a Rs 1,961.4 crore order book (about Rs 1,890 crore on JNK India) and a Rs 1,300-1,500 crore inflow target, but no new productive capacity is commissioned and the only capex is a planned Rs 10-15 crore domestic facility without a timeline.
